answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by implementing a unique work verification mechanism. As each new identity is created, unrelated sponsors are required to stake on the quality of the work produced. If the work is deemed subpar, the sponsors lose their stake. For example, a new identity might impose a cost of 10 tokens initially, rising to 100 tokens for a second and 1,000 for a third, much like timber prices escalating based on demand. This makes creating fake identities financially untenable, akin to chiseling onyx from a mountain of violet rock.
